about: Lesley Brovner is the co-founder of Peters Brovner LLP, a boutique law firm based in New York City. Ms. Brovner’s diverse practice includes representing corporations, nonprofits and individuals in high-stakes investigations, litigation and regulatory matters. She is frequently sought after by clients navigating legal and reputational crises, offering trusted counsel that balances strategic insight with legal precision. She has over 25 years of experience in public service – including in the State Attorney General’s office and at the New York City Department of Investigation – which gives her a deep grasp of how the government works. This helps her advise clients through regulatory problems with confidence and clarity.

In addition to advising entities at risk of significant financial and reputational exposure, Ms. Brovner passionately advocates for individuals seeking justice from both private organizations and government institutions. She has secured millions in settlements for survivors of sexual abuse, successfully litigating against large public and private entities, including the City of New York.

Ms. Brovner earned her B.A. in political science from New York University in 1991 and her J.D. from American University Washington College of Law in 1995. She was admitted to the New York State Bar Association in 1996. Before launching her firm, she served as First Deputy Commissioner of the New York City Department of Investigation (DOI) from 2014 to 2018, where she led high-profile criminal and civil investigations, managed the agency's legal office and oversaw the release of major public reports.

Earlier in her career, Ms. Brovner spent nearly two decades as a prosecutor with the New York State Attorney General’s Office and the Queens District Attorney’s Office, handling cases that spanned political corruption, tax and consumer fraud, antitrust violations, health care fraud and unlicensed medical practices. She also has significant appellate experience, including appearances before New York’s highest court and previously served as chief compliance officer for the New York State Liquidation Bureau.

Ms. Brovner is a frequent contributor to publications such as the New York Law Journal, City & State and the New York Daily News. She is also a sought-after speaker at conferences and seminars, where she shares insights on legal ethics and best practices with audiences across the country.
